newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rival state ready to team up with gov't.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rival state ready to team up with gov't.

text.p: The fundamentalist Moslem party controlling Malaysia's sole opposition state said on Monday it was prepared to team up with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's party to run northeastern Kelantan.
Kelantan's Chief Minister Nik Aziz Nik Mat said he was ready to consider any conditions laid down by Mahathir for a new coalition government in Kelantan, the national news agency Bernama said.

Nik Aziz's Parti Islam se-Malaysia (PAS) had governed the state in a coalition with the smaller Spirit of 46 until the latter decided to dissolve itself and join Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation last month.
Spirit's desertion has left Nik Aziz with a fragile minority in the state assembly.
"In any negotiations there are bound to be conditions," Nik Aziz said. "Once we hear their conditions, we will put forward our own conditions. If there is anything more then we can discuss further."
Kelantan, one of Malaysia's most economically-backward states, has been controlled since 1990 by PAS.

The party has laid down a series of measures since then to create a more Islamic society in the state, including bans on gambling, unisex hair saloons and amusement parks. It has also mandated separate supermarket lines for men and women and warned women against using too much make-up.
The stance is at odds with Mahathir's government, which urges a more tolerant brand of Islam in multiracial Malaysia.
Mahathir told reporters at the weekend he was open to forming a coalition government in Kelantan with PAS but added that the rival party should not demand too much from his government.
